title: Choose the visual world (round 2)
question: The re-roll assigned The Viewfinder. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll again.

options.label: The Viewfinder
options.lineage: Macro's meal scan turned on the engineer: a camera viewfinder reading a white page
options.thesis: A white page where one pair of scan brackets follows your cursor, snaps to whatever you point at, and reads it out: name, app, year, number.
materials: one ink blue for the brackets and the readout
regular-weight grotesk at 9–12vw on the first screen
options.viewport: Words only on the first screen: a two-line statement in my own voice at 10vw across the full width, one supporting sentence bottom-left, Email me bottom-right. The brackets sit around the first word and move to whatever you hover; the readout under them says what it is.
options.risk: A cursor effect that becomes a gimmick if the brackets do not also work on a phone (there they snap to the section in view) and if the readouts say nothing real.

raised.raise: Every role and project carries its running time, right-aligned tight against the margin, so the list reads like a tracklist that adds up.
Entries sit at one fixed scale on one shared baseline; nothing on the page is bigger because it is newer.
The brackets' readout is a measurement: a number, a year, a platform, never a slogan.
When the brackets lock on something, everything else holds still; motion lives only in the thing being read.

options.label: The Demo-day Deck
options.lineage: the founder's pitch slide: one claim, one number, full screen
options.thesis: The page as the deck I would pitch with: each screen one claim in huge type with one figure, paged with the keyboard or a scroll snap.
options.viewport: Slide one: 'I build apps people actually use.' and nothing else; a pager at the bottom edge.
options.risk: Also the direction most founder portfolios reach for; the pager and snap can fight the scroll on phones.

options.label: Cassette J-card
options.thesis: The CV as a ballpoint tracklist timed to the minute.
options.viewport: A folded card; side A and side B.
options.case: Hiring managers do not identify with mixtapes; handwriting fights a minimal brief.
options.kept: Running times right-aligned against the margin.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: The career as five plates of one plant.
options.case: Cream and hairline rules are the look the brief excludes, and plants say nothing about shipping software.
options.kept: Fixed scale on one shared baseline.

options.label: Blacksmith Scale Shower
options.thesis: Each job as a hammer blow.
options.case: Dark and loud; you asked for light and minimal.
options.kept: Readings as numbers, before and after.

options.label: Cracktro Scroller
options.thesis: Bitmap text drifting over a void.
options.viewport: One line of bitmap text, dust drifting behind.
options.case: A black void is the opposite of the light page you asked for.
options.kept: Focus freezes the front plane; motion only where you are reading.

options.label: Seven-segment Display
options.kept: Absence drawn as deliberately as presence.

options.label: Hand-bent Neon
options.thesis: The name as one continuous glass stroke.
options.case: Dark, and glow is banned by the brief.
options.kept: One continuous element moves as a single stroke.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The developer portfolio everyone ships: white page, name, one line, project cards, skills, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Name and one sentence, a button, cards below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other candidate's site.
